memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "But I will harden Pharaoh's heart, and though I multiply my signs and wonders in Egypt, he will not listen to you. Then I will lay my hand on Egypt and with mighty acts of judgment I will bring out my divisions, my people the Israelites." - Exodus 7:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God tells Moses plainly what to expect: the signs will come, and Pharaoh still will not listen.

This is the hard theme of Exodus, and we handle it carefully. Scripture says God hardened Pharaoh's heart, and it also says Pharaoh hardened his own heart. Both are stated, and the Bible sees no contradiction. Pharaoh was never forced to do anything he did not want to do. He was a proud man who had already ordered the drowning of babies, and God confirmed him in the path he had freely chosen. That is judgement, not injustice.

Believers who love the Bible have long differed on exactly how divine sovereignty and human choice fit together, and a devotional will not settle it. What Scripture states without hesitation is that God is just, God is never the author of evil, and God's purposes cannot be defeated.

The practical warning is the one we must not miss. Hearts harden gradually, through repeated resistance. Scripture urges us: today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts (Heb 3:15).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where have I been repeatedly resisting something God has made clear?
2. Am I willing to trust God's justice where I cannot fully understand His ways?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep my heart soft. Where I have been resisting You, break through before I grow harder still. Amen.
